tool.name: VariableContinuation
tool.summary: Continue a grid from the surface it was measured on to another surface, either of them uneven (Cordell & Grauch 1985): e.g. a draped survey to a constant height above sea level, or a barometric survey to a constant clearance above the topography.
tool.usage:
Each surface is Baro (constant height): a constant height above sea level, as a barometric survey; Drape (height grid): a grid of heights above sea level, e.g. a draped survey's GPS altitude; or Drape (DEM + clearance): a DEM plus the clearance given. Height grids and DEMs are resampled onto the input grid.

Observed = Drape, Output = Baro levels a draped survey to a constant height; Observed = Baro, Output = Drape (DEM + clearance) drapes a barometric survey over the topography.

Uneven data are flattened onto the level of their lowest point by an iteration that needs no damping, continued to the mean height of the output surface, then draped onto an uneven output surface by Taylor series. Only downward continuation is damped (Smoothing Wavelength).

A warning is given if the output surface, or a constant observed height, is below the topography (when a DEM is given), or a clearance is negative.

The same calculation as the SGTool QGIS plugin's Continuation, direction variable.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: obs_surface
param.dialogReference: The surface the data were measured on: Baro (constant height), Drape (height grid) or Drape (DEM + clearance).
param.pythonReference: The surface the data were measured on: Baro (constant height), Drape (height grid) or Drape (DEM + clearance).

param.name: obs_grid
param.dialogReference: Height grid or DEM of the observed surface (m above sea level), for the two kinds of drape.
param.pythonReference: Height grid or DEM of the observed surface (m above sea level), for the two kinds of drape.

param.name: obs_value
param.dialogReference: Constant height above sea level (m), or the clearance above the DEM (m).
param.pythonReference: Constant height above sea level (m), or the clearance above the DEM (m).

param.name: out_surface
param.dialogReference: The surface to continue the data onto: Baro (constant height), Drape (height grid) or Drape (DEM + clearance).
param.pythonReference: The surface to continue the data onto: Baro (constant height), Drape (height grid) or Drape (DEM + clearance).

param.name: out_grid
param.dialogReference: Height grid or DEM of the output surface (m above sea level), for the two kinds of drape.
param.pythonReference: Height grid or DEM of the output surface (m above sea level), for the two kinds of drape.

param.name: out_value
param.dialogReference: Constant height above sea level (m), or the clearance above the DEM (m).
param.pythonReference: Constant height above sea level (m), or the clearance above the DEM (m).

param.name: smoothing
param.dialogReference: Wavelength (m) below which downward continuation and the draping series are damped. 0 = automatic: pi x the output surface's relief, and enough to keep the gain of downward continuation below about 20. Not used when the output is above all the observations.
param.pythonReference: Wavelength (m) below which downward continuation and the draping series are damped. 0 = automatic: pi x the output surface's relief, and enough to keep the gain of downward continuation below about 20. Not used when the output is above all the observations.

param.name: terms
param.dialogReference: Number of terms (vertical derivatives) in the Taylor series that drapes the result onto an uneven output surface (1-12).
param.pythonReference: Number of terms (vertical derivatives) in the Taylor series that drapes the result onto an uneven output surface (1-12).
